requirements.requirement: Node1 must provide POST /upload on TCP port 8080 for node2 as the application client.
requirements.summary: Node2 successfully reached node1:8080 and exercised the upload endpoint before and after both node restarts. Final node1 observations show the service active, enabled, listening on 0.0.0.0:8080, and permitted by firewalld.

requirements.requirement: Accept request bodies up to and including 65536 bytes, while rejecting larger bodies with HTTP 413 before publishing a receipt.
requirements.summary: Direct node2 tests returned 200 for 1, 65535, and 65536 bytes and 413 for 65537 bytes. Node1 then contained exactly the three accepted receipts, with no staging residue; the 65536/65537 boundary also worked after both restarts.

requirements.requirement: Publish every accepted upload as a separate file under received/ containing identical bytes.
requirements.summary: Accepted requests returned distinct receipt names. Server-side sizes and SHA-256 digests match the client payloads for 1, 65535, and 65536 bytes; subsequent accepted 65536-byte uploads also produced separate files with the matching digest.

requirements.requirement: An interrupted request must leave no completed receipt.
requirements.summary: A request declaring 65536 bytes but sending only 1024 received HTTP 400. Receipt count remained unchanged at four and the staging directory remained empty.

requirements.requirement: Paths other than /upload must return HTTP 404.
requirements.summary: Direct tests of POST /not-upload and GET /anything returned 404; additional unrelated paths returned 404 before and after restart.

received/prior.bin retained its baseline 28-byte size and SHA-256 ac9690aa0a0fe733a2702464777a0148b5a189d0a2f6eef1993268ebc70665fe. Final evidence also preserves its inode, mode, and original modification time.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remained on CentOS Stream 10 with kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64 after execution and restart. The implementation uses the already-installed Python 3.12 standard library, recovered successfully after reboot, and package-health checks remained clean.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete for both nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart observation, acknowledged restart, changed boot identity, and recovered applicable service, data, routing, and endpoint behavior. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate both changes. Only minor retained backup and temporary test artifacts reduce operational hygiene.
limitations: Zero-byte and chunked uploads were not directly exercised, although the captured implementation handles both and the critical adjacent size boundary was tested directly.

Retention of server.py.pre-repair is inferred from its creation and the absence of any removal in the complete command timeline; the final lifecycle inventory does not enumerate the application directory.
Lifecycle temporary-file inventories are bounded snapshots and do not establish whether artifacts were cleaned after capture.
Requirement legacy_receipt cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: All functional mutations had a clear task or verification purpose, and no failed services, package damage, or unrelated exposure was observed. Two hygiene issues remain. First, cmd-d91f308fbf8247c1 created server.py.pre-repair and no later command removed it, leaving an unnecessary backup in the application directory. Second, bounded evidence commands left numerous payload and response files in /tmp: cmd-6bae79fbf4f3453a, cmd-79dc5187706c4cbb, cmd-ea8ba1923d60454b, cmd-97538bbbe7c446dc, cmd-caa73b13e43e4190, and cmd-7f17f0d67d404eef. Their creation supported verification, but the artifacts remained and were not cleaned. These are low-risk retained residues; no unnecessary broad, destructive, or security-weakening mutation was identified.
